findings.reason: without a followup the section is dispatchable only from a coordinator's memory, which is exactly the state that produced the wiring findings on §19, §20 and §21 in earlier rounds of this review, each of which was acted on.
findings.text: §24 is the only work left on the plan beside §6, and no followup carries it: the followup list ends at `f-awcwyh-023` (:1655 region, both it and `f-awcwyh-022` now resolved), and `grep -c '§24'` over the whole snapshot returns 1, the section's own heading — so there is no `/reckon-build … §24` entry point and the roadmap has no record of the section

findings.reason: the deliverable and its assertion stand; a node needs only to separate the index write from the edit by more than a second, which is a test detail rather than a change to what is built.
findings.text: the control "edits a tracked file while keeping its size and restoring its mtime, and asserts `git diff --name-only` still names it" leaves ctime as the only discriminator, and `core.checkStat=minimal` compares ctime at whole-second resolution, so an index written and a file edited inside the same second read clean and the control fails on correct code

findings.reason: the done-when asserts the effective value in each tree, which holds either way, and the node writes the extension regardless; only the sentence overstates the isolation.
findings.text: "so the main checkout's configuration is unchanged" is not what the prescribed mechanism does: a worktree-scoped config exists only after `extensions.worktreeConfig=true` is written into the shared `.git/config`, measured here on git 2.39.3, so the shared configuration does change while the shared `core.checkStat` does not
